visualLanguage: design_system/public/PUBLIC_UI.md patterns, built from components/site/v3. No KB-era mockup: the pattern set is the target, the same basis as every post-2026-08-27 page. Broadside register (a page that shows, not a search surface).
competitiveTarget: Beat the portals and the local commercial brokers on a page a search engine can rank for 'commercial space for lease Bend'. The consumer portals are built for homes; the commercial listing sites file leases behind search state, and a local commercial broker's site shows that broker's own. This page lists every active commercial lease on the regional MLS in Central Oregon, grouped by town, each one a door to its own page, with the asking rent in its own unit (per sq ft per month, per month, per year) and never a bare number, and a Ryan Realty broker one tap away.
note: Matt 2026-09-23 approved the lease section on place pages and this page with it. One read, getCommercialLeaseListings: listing_tile_mv PropertyType G, Active and Active Under Contract, MLS City in the service-area allowlist, plus each lease's rent unit from listings.details 'Lease Rate Options' (getLeaseRateOptions). Counted 2026-09-23: 36 leases, Bend 13, Redmond 12, Prineville 4, Madras 3, Sisters 3, Powell Butte 1. The rent prints through publishLeaseRate: with its unit, or 'Lease rate not published' when the unit is missing, unknown, or contradicted by the number (a per sq ft rate of $100 or more, a whole-space amount under $100; the feed has nothing between $36 and $325). A lease is never an Offer: the ItemList names each lease and its rent in words and has no price property. The dials are V3PlaceInventory layout='dial', the same primitive and card as the 'Commercial space for lease' section on a place page (TASTE: two sections doing one job are one primitive); since 2026-09-30 only the busiest town leads on a full dial and every other town is a drawer row that opens to its own dial or rows, so the page reads as a market browsed from its biggest town down and not six identical blocks. An empty pull opts out of ISR and says 'Nothing listed on this refresh', never that no space exists.

requiredComponents.name: V3Breadcrumb
requiredComponents.section: Chrome. Home > Commercial space for lease.

requiredComponents.name: V3Ledger
requiredComponents.section: #towns: the opening and the H1. One row per town with a lease, its count drawn as a length (encode='bar') and the square feet its spaces list drawn as a line under it on its own scale (the row's `also`, keyed over the rows by `encodeKey`; the sentence says how many list no size), its rate line under the name (publishLeaseRateSummary: one span per rent unit with how many leases use it, and how many rates are not published, so the line covers every lease the count does), a hover that reveals its sizes, one of its own leases pictured, each row a door to that town's leases. The lease map is its drawing (beside the rows from 64rem, after the rows below it, so a phone's first screen shows the bars its sentence describes), and its one action is the page's ask: 'Tell a broker the space you need', the contact form filed as a commercial-lease inquiry.

requiredComponents.name: V3PlaceInventory
requiredComponents.section: #lease: the busiest town on its own full V3ListingDial (leaseTownTiers' lead), then the drawer of every other town (its `after` slot), then the block's one source line. Every dial opens on the largest space whose rent publishes (leaseRowsLargestFirst: rents that publish first, then by listed size, largest first), a rule that holds as listings change, never a picked listing. The lease card: rent with its unit, 'For lease', terms; every lease an <a href> in the served HTML.

requiredComponents.name: LeaseMap
requiredComponents.section: #lease-map, the ledger's drawing (2026-09-30, 'no map on a page about geography'): server-drawn, no client code. Every lease a dot at its listing's own coordinates, sized by its listed square feet (a ring when it lists none), a door to its page with the card's rent line on hover or focus; each town's name and count beside its dots, the same door as its ledger row; highways and rivers from the repo's TIGER/Line 2024 basemap. Hovering a row lights its town here and the other way round (lease-page.css). Not V3Atlas: the Atlas counts 'for sale' and prints price pills and medians, which a rent in four units cannot be.

requiredComponents.name: LeaseTownDrawer
requiredComponents.section: #lease-more, inside #lease: every other town, busiest first, each a <section> named by its <h2>, its row a <details> (the first open). The rows are one drawing: each town's rents on ONE shared axis of asking rent per sq ft per month (leaseRentStrips: a dot per lease filed and published in that unit, sized by its listed square feet, a ring when it lists none; no other unit is converted onto it), its rate line one unit to a line (every lease it counts), and its largest listed space photographed with its size and street (leaseTownLargest), then a toggle, opening on demand to its own V3ListingDial (5 leases or more) or its leases as V3ListingRow cards (rent with its unit, 'For lease', size, street, terms). A link to a town's anchor opens its row. Every lease is an <a href> in the served HTML, open or not.

requiredComponents.name: V3Quiet
requiredComponents.section: #edges: the towns' own pages, homes for sale, a broker. Also the empty-pull H1 branch, where it replaces the Ledger and the dials.

requiredComponents.name: V3Footer
requiredComponents.section: Chrome. Rendered OUTSIDE <main> so the footer maps to contentinfo.

tasteReview.beats: LoopNet's Central Oregon commercial-lease search: this page wins on data depth (per-town rate ranges, total sq ft, a sourced map with size-coded dots, honest 'rate not published' / 'size not listed' labeling) and on clarity (town-as-unit instead of an unsorted listing grid). LoopNet still wins on raw inventory count and saved-search/alert tooling.

defects.section: town ledger rows (bars view + turned dot-strip view)
defects.finding: The same six towns and the same facts (lease count, rate range, sq ft) are rendered twice at full length down the page — once as horizontal bars on the fold, again as per-town dot strips in the 'turned' section. The second pass adds no new fact, just a different mark, so it reads as two chart ideas shipped side by side rather than one confident view with a toggle.

Listing thumbnails inside each town row vary wildly in crop, light, and quality (a tight blue-sky warehouse exterior next to a dim near-black interior sliver for Redmond, a flat daylight shot for Sisters), which undercuts the editorial consistency the hairlines, tabular numerals, and sourced captions otherwise earn.

Each town header in the dot-strip view repeats an identical chevron-dropdown box six times down the page with no visible state difference between rows beyond the label, especially at 375px where four near-identical chevron boxes stack with little to distinguish one town's control from the next — it reads as decoration until an open state proves otherwise.

tasteReview.verdict: This is the house-ledger and house-listing forms built correctly with real interaction — hover links a bar to its map pin and reveals a size range, a toggle swaps bar length for a price dot-strip, and the per-listing dial carries a working filmstrip — so demoMatch is true and nothing here is a cream box. It clears the banned tells (a custom-styled map, no KPI grid, sourced captions, no wall of text) and the honesty bar is genuinely strong, but it spends a full second section re-stating the same six facts in a different mark instead of adding one, and the row thumbnails are inconsistent enough to dent the editorial polish. Competent, original data journalism for a commercial-lease page — rare for this category — but not yet the one idea confident enough to screenshot.
tasteReview.dullest: The per-town rows themselves — thumbnail, three lines of rate copy, a bar — repeated six times, then repeated again forty pixels later as a dot cluster on the same axis. Once you've read 'Bend: 13 for lease' as a bar, the second reading as a dot strip tells you nothing new.

contentFloor.note: No-regression floor (ci:route-content-floor). A build under any number here fails before the evaluator runs. Lower a number only by hand, in the same commit, with the reason. Section depth (contentFloor.floors.sectionDepth) follows the same rule. Seeded 2026-09-24 by `node scripts/check-route-content-floor.mjs --seed http://127.0.0.1:3465 --classes commercial-space-for-lease` against agent/lease-floor's dev server reading the live project (36 leases: Bend 13, Redmond 12, Prineville 4, Madras 3, Sisters 3, Powell Butte 1). Every number is the tool's except the two hero floors, set by hand at seed (the tool wrote 835 and 576). This page has NO photographic hero by design: it opens on the #towns ledger as the H1. The widest image in the gate's first-1200px window is the Bend dial's lead photograph, whose top measured 1167px, 33px inside the window, so one more town row or one more two-line rate line moves it out and the header wordmark (logo-horizontal-navy-transparent.png, 120px rendered, 2271 natural) wins, the root cause of the six re-seeds in 3a151e4e5. And that lead's resolution is Spark's per-photo derivative of the sanctioned 800x600 bucket, which on this page's own 36 lead photographs measured 360 to 1140 natural (360 on three leases; the Bend lead read 640). heroImageWidth 108 = floor(120 * 0.9), the wordmark, as on oregon-city, place-type-community, cities, search and reviews. heroImageNatural 324 = floor(360 * 0.9), the smallest lead derivative this page carries today: every lead and the wordmark clear it, and the banned 320x240 ledger thumb (320 natural) still fails. The page's photographs are also held by images (12 loaded at 800px natural or wider, floor 8) and the dials by sectionDepth.lease words. LOWERED BY HAND 2026-09-25, images 8 -> 5, in the listing-dial integration commit: the dial now serves a card that is not showing as its door alone (the link with its rent, facts and street; its photograph mounts when the card turns up, V3ListingDial weight rule, about 1 KB of HTML per listing), so the gate, which forces every lazy eager, no longer finds a hidden card's photograph to load. The integrated build read images 6: one lead photograph per town dial, the same photographs a reader sees on arrival. No photograph left the page; each still loads on its turn. Floor 5 = the towns floor (sectionDepth.towns.items 5), one lead per town.
